newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: U.S. offers Switzerland trade talks on MRAs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. offers Switzerland trade talks on MRAs.

text.p: The United States on Monday offered to begin talks with Switzerland on a series of Mutual Recognition Agreements (MRAs) that could cover some 10 percent of the countries' annual bilateral trade.
Negotiations on removing technical barriers to trade are expected to begin in Washington D.C. in September, the U.S. embassy said in a statement.
"This offer is a clear indication of the importance the United States attaches to close relations with Switzerland," the statement quoted Ambassador Madeleine Kunin as saying.

The U.S. and the European Union (EU) recently concluded discussions on MRAs that cover speed boats, telecommunications products, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, electromagnetic compatibility and electrical safety.
Under MRAs, each country recognises the results of each other's testing, inspection and manufacturing standards.
Delegations from the United States and Switzerland will consider which products should be included in the agreements.
The United States is the second largest market for Swiss exports, which amounted to $8.0 billion in 1996. U.S. exported goods worth $8.4 billion to Switzerland.
